correctness.summary: The Simes rejection event is exactly determined by the four threshold bins A=(0,r], B=(r,2r], C=(2r,3r], D=(3r,1] with r=α/3. Pairwise independence fixes the ten second-factorial/category moments. The three displayed quadratic certificates were checked on all 20 occupancy types, and the three exchangeable occupancy constructions satisfy normalization, all ten pair laws, nonnegativity on their stated parameter ranges, and the claimed rejection polynomials. Conditional independent uniformization inside the bins preserves both pairwise independence and the event. An independent linear-program reconstruction over all 20 exchangeable occupancy states matched the claimed envelope at representative points in every branch and at the breakpoints α=3/5 and 3/4.

originality.summary: Simes (1986) treats mutual independence. Ramachandra–Natarajan develop tight pairwise-independent Bernoulli probability bounds, but their accessible paper does not formulate the Simes ordered-p-value problem. Hommel (1983) was retrieved in full through authorized institutional access after open routes did not yield the full text; it studies three overall-test constructions under arbitrary dependence (Bonferroni, Rüger, and a modification), predates Simes, and does not contain the three-uniform-p-value pairwise-independent envelope. Targeted searches found no prior statement of the exact three-p-value piecewise curve or these extremizers.

scientific_value.summary: Pairwise independence is a natural intermediate dependence regime. The record gives the exact finite-sample worst-case size, not just a counterexample, and its global-null equivalence immediately gives the sharp three-hypothesis BH FDR envelope.

citations.title: Simes, An improved Bonferroni procedure for multiple tests of significance (1986)
Hommel, Tests of the Overall Hypothesis for Arbitrary Dependence Structures (1983)
Ramachandra and Natarajan, Tight Probability Bounds with Pairwise Independence
Benjamini and Hochberg, Controlling the False Discovery Rate (1995)

limitations: The exact envelope is only for three exactly uniform null p-values; m>=4, super-uniform nonuniform nulls and partial-null configurations are not solved.
Equivalent formulations in older Bonferroni/copula/extremal-probability literature remain possible despite the targeted search.
Hommel (1983) was inspected in full via authorized institutional access; no claim is made about inaccessible literature beyond the sources actually retrieved.
